title: Graph Valid Tree
description: There are `n` nodes labelled `0` to `n - 1` and a list of undirected `edges`. Return `true` if these edges make the nodes form a **tree**: the graph is connected and contains no cycle.
constraints: No duplicate edges and no self-loops
hints: A tree on n nodes has a very specific number of edges. What is it?
If edges.length != n - 1 you can answer false immediately. With exactly n - 1 edges, connected and acyclic become equivalent.
Union-find: merge edge endpoints and fail if both are already in the same set; or run a DFS from node 0 and check that all n nodes are visited.

solution.explanation: A tree on n nodes has exactly n - 1 edges, so any other edge count is an immediate false. With n - 1 edges, the graph is a tree if and only if it has no cycle, which union-find detects: if an edge joins two nodes already in the same set, we found a cycle. If no cycle appears, n - 1 successful merges connect everything. Time is nearly linear in the number of edges; space is O(n).
